newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's co-op banks to launch pre-paid cards.
newsitem.headline: Germany's co-op banks to launch pre-paid cards.

text.p: Germany's co-operative banks are this year to issue six million plastic payment cards which can function as "electronic purses", the cooperative banking association (BVR) said on Thursday.

Taking their lead from large commercial banks such as Deutsche Bank and Commerzbank, the BVR said its members had already started issuing the cards and would complete the issue by the end of December.

Pre-paid cards, still a novelty in Germany but spreading fast, have an inbuilt micro-chip which allows holders to load them at special machines with a fixed cash value, usually about 400 marks ($263), and use them to pay for small-ticket items.
The BVR's card also functions as an ordinary Eurocheque card, with the usual cash withdrawal and debit functions.

The BVR, which has a huge branch network in all German regions, said it expected pre-paid cards to establish a hold on the German market very quickly, and said all its discussions so far on their use had yielded surprisingly good responses.
Both Commerzbank and Deutsche are planning full launches of their versions of reloadable cards next year, following recent trials.
